sections.label: Mandatory rental waiver framework bill
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a legislative framework to implement mandatory two-week rental waivers by landlords for qualifying tenants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Minister for Finance announced in his Ministerial Statement on 26 July this year that the Government would provide an additional two weeks of direct rental support for qualifying tenants and owner-occupiers of privately-owned commercial properties.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Minister for Finance also said that the Government would consider requiring landlords to provide a matching two-week rental waiver for eligible tenants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: This Bill introduces the legislative framework to implement the mandatory rental waiver by the landlords.

sections.label: Two billion rental support
sections.summary: Over $2 billion is set aside for Phase Two (Heightened Alert), with eligible tenants receiving two weeks' gross rent waiver from landlords.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In total, more than $2 billion has been set aside to cushion the business impact of Phase Two (Heightened Alert).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Eligible tenants will receive from their landlords two weeks' waiver of gross rent, including service and maintenance charges.

sections.label: Rental waiver eligibility and procedure
sections.summary: The framework requires private commercial landlords to give qualifying tenants two weeks' waiver, with tenants showing a 20% income drop and submitting documents within 28 days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Under today's Bill, the Government is introducing the new rental waiver framework, which will require all private commercial landlords to provide two weeks of rental waiver to qualifying tenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Under the rental waiver framework, eligible tenants will receive a total of about one and a half month's of rental support, for which a month's rental support comes from the Government's Rental Support Scheme announced earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Tenants who wish to claim the rental waiver must, among other requirements, show that they have suffered a drop of at least 20% in their income for the two Phase Two (Heightened Alert) periods in May to June and August 2021 as compared to the Phase Three period between December 2020 and May 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Procedurally, tenants will be required to send a copy of their notice, a completed declaration form and the supporting documents to their immediate landlord via email or registered post within 28 days.

sections.label: Clarification on income evidence
sections.summary: The Member asks how stringent the documentary requirement is and whether alternative evidence of income drop is accepted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: To seek external help for a claim of just half a month's rental waiver may not be cost-effective to many micro businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, like to seek clarification with the Minister as to how stringent is this documentary requirement to show evidence of a drop in income and whether it is restricted to the businesses' profit and loss statements properly drawn up or the Ministry will be open to alternative evidence showing the drop in business income compared to previous months.

sections.label: Support for SMEs rental relief
sections.summary: The Member supports the Bill, citing SME pressure and the framework letting an Assessor determine rental waiver allocations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: My concern is that the SMEs, especially the micro SMEs, may still feel business pressure and lower sales arising from the SMMs and challenges of COVID-19 generally and may struggle more with their business rentals as compared to other more established or bigger businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I rise in support of this Bill as it sets out the rental relief framework for tenants so that an Assessor can cost effectively and efficiently determine rental waiver allocations between the landlords and tenants, and those down the tenancy chain.

sections.label: Measures for less savvy tenants
sections.summary: The Government considered last year's experience and put in place measures to help less savvy tenants navigate the framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim's question on less savvy tenants and how can they navigate the framework more easily, we have considered the experience from last year and put in place some measures.

sections.label: Informing parties along PTO chain
sections.summary: The party making the application must inform all parties along the PTO chain.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On Mr Zhulkarnain's other question, we are making it mandatory for the party making the application to inform all parties along the PTO chain.

sections.label: Statutory declaration for business downturn
sections.summary: The law allows businesses to swear a statutory declaration that their business has gone down by the required amount and attach evidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The law allows – and this is not the first piece of legislation; previous COVID-19 legislation as well – them to swear a statutory declaration that their business has gone down by the required amount and attach whatever evidence they have.
